items.prompt: 原题 Step 3：STEP 3: Organize your ideas.
items.instruction: 把立场写成初步thesis；选择point-by-point或block，为己方论证与反方回应列提纲。
items.answer: 本步记录：中心论点+组织方式+各段功能/论点/证据/反驳位置。
items.explanation: block按两大部分集中安排；point-by-point每个争点同时处理双方。无论哪种，读者都应能追踪你的最终立场。
items.sourceLabel: 教材第165–167页，写作流程Step 3；开放任务无固定标准全文。
rubric: thesis明确可争辩。
提纲实际安排双方与回应。
各段顺序与所选组织方式一致。

items.prompt: 原题 Step 4：STEP 4: Write the first draft.
items.instruction: 引言框定问题与双方争论；主体逐项发展主张，用例子、事实、数据、来源引文支撑；按本章方法回应反方；结尾回到总论点，并可提出行动呼吁。
items.answer: 开放初稿。完整文本应有引言、主体、结论；来源资料与自己的分析相互连接；对反方至少作一处实质回应。
items.explanation: 这一步要提交真正的文章草稿，只有提纲不能代替。来源的事实和引语必须可追溯。

missions.instructions: 原限时50分钟：读题并写thesis 5分钟；头脑风暴/提纲5分钟；写文章30分钟；检查改错10分钟；如课程要求交老师。Writing Tip：起草早期可先用短注记标出待放支撑材料的位置，后续补入，不能在成稿中留下无证据的占位。
missions.answerNote: 开放写作，无提供标准作文；按立场、支撑、反方回应与语言自评。

items.prompt: 原题 Timed Writing：Should the current grading practices in your school be altered or remain the same? If you think they should change, how should they change, and what effects would these changes have?
items.instruction: 依50分钟流程写完整短议论文：引言框定争议，主体支持主要理由并回应反方。若主张改变，必须说明怎样改变及影响；若主张保持，论证理由。
items.answer: 开放限时作文。可支持改变或保持，但要正面回答全部题干；观点需要具体理由、对反方的回应与清楚结论。若无可核实数据，可用明确标识的个人观察或逻辑推理，不编造调查。
items.explanation: 原题不仅问“赞不赞成”，还追问改变方式与影响；写改革方案却不分析后果属于答题不完整。

items.prompt: 原题 1：How many sentences are there in the original passage? In the paraphrase?
items.instruction: 阅读完整模型，回答所有子问，可用中文解释并保留所指英文词。
items.answer: 原文5句；改写6句。
items.explanation: 按句号数完整陈述。改写可以拆句，并非必须保持原句数量。
items.sourceLabel: 教材第128页；配套答案册第25–26页（PDF 1–2）。
items.passage:
Original Passage
Language is the main means of communication between peoples. But so many different languages have developed that language has often been a barrier rather than an aid to understanding among peoples. For many years, people have dreamed of setting up an international universal language which all people could speak and understand. The arguments in favor of a universal language are simple and obvious. If all peoples spoke the same tongue, cultural and economic ties might be much closer, and good will might increase between countries (Kispert).

Paraphrase
Humans communicate through language. Because there are so many different languages, however, people around the world have a difficult time understanding one another. Some people have wished for a universal international language that speakers all over the world could understand. Their reasons are straightforward and clear. A universal language would build cultural and economic bonds. It would also create better feelings among countries (Kispert).

Source: Kispert, Robert J. “Universal language.” World Book Online Reference Center. 2004. World Book, Inc. 13 Nov. 2004. 原教材来源标注。
rubric: 分别回答原文5句、改写6句，不能只写一个数字。
以完整句的终止标点计数，不把分号当成另起一句。

items.prompt: 原题 模型写作题：Television programming in the United States is often criticized for promoting the wrong values. Do you agree or disagree with this criticism?
items.instruction: 把教材已完成示范恢复为独立练习：围绕原写作题写一个段落，使用所给来源的改写作支撑，说明来源与你的立场的联系，并加文内引用。
items.answer: 教材示范段落（不是唯一答案）：Although it is sometimes true that television programming in the United States promotes the wrong values, I do not entirely agree. Many educational television channels promote good values. For example, the Discovery Channel, the History Channel, National Geographic, and other similar channels educate the public about science, history, nature, and the environment. Also, even prime-time television programming often provides a public service by spreading public service messages. In fact, environmental messages have been deliberately put into prime-time television shows for the past decade. Environmental Media Association, an organization of professionals in the entertainment business, encourages television actors, writers, directors, and producers to promote environmentalism in three ways: by using environmental issues in scripts, by using environmental products as props, and by making environmentally conscious choices in studios (Leroux, par. 2). Seeing the star of a prime-time television show recycling plastic bottles or using an environmentally friendly product is more persuasive than almost any other type of public service message. In short, television programs promote positive values in both direct and indirect ways.
items.explanation: 示范先承认部分批评，再说明教育节目与黄金时段环保信息的正面作用。引用后还有解释：节目明星的环保行为为什么能影响观众。不要把引用堆成整段。

For 10 years, the Environmental Media Association (EMA) has been working to weave the environment into prime-time television programming. Created by and for professionals in the entertainment industry, EMA works with the stars in front of the cameras as well as the creative staff behind them to include environmental themes in scripts, show environmental products on sets, and make environmentally sound decisions in the studios.
rubric: 明确同意、反对或部分同意，且段内一致。
真正改写EMA来源，引用(Leroux, par. 2)。
自己解释证据为何支持主张，并有收束句。

items.prompt: 原题 1：How many sentences are there in the original passage? In the paraphrase? In the summary?
items.instruction: 分别填写三份文本的句子数。
items.answer: 原文5句；改写6句；摘要2句。
items.explanation: 摘要删减细节，只保留语言差异形成障碍、通用语言可能促进联系这两个核心层次。
items.sourceLabel: 教材第137页；答案册第25–26页。
items.passage:
Original Passage
Language is the main means of communication between peoples. But so many different languages have developed that language has often been a barrier rather than an aid to understanding among peoples. For many years, people have dreamed of setting up an international universal language which all people could speak and understand. The arguments in favor of a universal language are simple and obvious. If all peoples spoke the same tongue, cultural and economic ties might be much closer, and good will might increase between countries (Kispert).

Paraphrase
Humans communicate through language. Because there are so many different languages, however, people around the world have a difficult time understanding one another. Some people have wished for a universal international language that speakers all over the world could understand. Their reasons are straightforward and clear. A universal language would build cultural and economic bonds. It would also create better feelings among countries (Kispert).

Summary
People communicate through language; however, having different languages creates communication barriers. A universal language could bring countries together culturally and economically as well as increase good feelings among them (Kispert).
rubric: 按原文、改写、摘要的顺序写5、6、2。
三个文本都计数，不把分号分隔的部分算成两个句子。

items.prompt: 原题 2：Compare the paraphrase and the summary. What two details were left out of the summary?

items.answer: 省去：Some people have wished for a universal international language that speakers all over the world could understand. 以及 Their reasons are straightforward and clear.

A universal language would build cultural and economic bonds. It would also create better feelings among countries (Kispert).

Summary
People communicate through language; however, having different languages creates communication barriers. A universal language could bring countries together culturally and economically as well as increase good feelings among them (Kispert).

items.prompt: 原题 1：Which of the two is the better summary? Why?
items.instruction: 写A或B并解释为什么更适合作摘要。
items.answer: Summary B更好：只保留原文主要观点；Summary A几乎与原文一样长，还加入了来源没有的信息。
items.explanation: B保留“语言技术障碍、正在改善、商业动机、保护濒危语言”四层主干。A重复很多细节；此外把every two weeks误写成every day，也是信息准确性问题。

items.passage:
Source: Marc Lacey, “Using a New Language in Africa to Save Dying Ones.” New York Times, November 12, 2004, page A3.

Original Passage
Swahili speakers wishing to use a “compyuta”—as computer is rendered in Swahili—have been out of luck when it comes to communicating in their tongue. Computers, no matter how bulky their hard drives or sophisticated their software packages, have not yet mastered Swahili or hundreds of other indigenous African languages. But that may soon change. Across the continent, linguists are working with experts in information technology to make computers more accessible to Africans who happen not to know English, French, or the other major languages that have been programmed into the world’s desktops. There are economic reasons for the outreach. Microsoft, which is working to incorporate Swahili into Microsoft Windows, Microsoft Office, and other popular programs, sees a market for its software among the roughly 100 million Swahili speakers in East Africa. The same goes for Google, which last month launched www.google.co.ke, offering a Kenyan version in Swahili of the popular search engine. But the campaign to Africanize cyberspace is not all about the bottom line. There are hundreds of languages in Africa—some spoken only by a few dozen elders—and they are dying out at an alarming rate. The continent's linguists see the computers as one important way of saving them. UNESCO estimates that 90 percent of the world's 6,000 languages are not represented on the Internet and that one language disappears somewhere around the world every two weeks.

Summary A
People who speak Swahili who want to communicate using a “compyuta,” which is the Swahili word for computer, are unable to do so in their own language. It makes no difference that computers have huge hard drives and sophisticated software. They cannot operate in Swahili or other African languages, of which there are hundreds. Soon, however, they may be able to. Linguists in Africa are working with information technology specialists to make computers operable to Africans who do not know any of the languages currently used on the Internet. Economics is bringing about this change. Microsoft sees a market for its software among Swahili speakers in East Africa. Google now has a search engine for speakers of Swahili in Kenya. Other software companies will probably soon develop products for African consumers. In addition to economics, there is another reason for making the computer accessible to Africans. Hundreds of African languages are dying out, and linguists view the computer as a way to save them. According to UNESCO estimates, 90 percent of the world's 6,000 languages are not on the Internet, and one language becomes extinct every day somewhere in the world. The hope is that computers can help save them (Lacey).

Summary B
Many Africans who do not speak any of the major languages on the Internet have been unable to use computers in their native languages. Computers cannot yet accommodate languages such as Swahili. However, that situation may soon change. Linguists and computer experts are working to develop computers that work in Swahili and other African languages. Economics is one reason for doing so. Computer companies such as Microsoft and Google see a potentially huge market for its products in Africa. Another important reason is to save languages that are in danger of becoming extinct (Lacey).
rubric: 选择B。
说明应概括主旨和主要支撑，而不是尽量保留全部细节。

items.prompt: 原题 2：Which summary contains an idea that was not in the original? Which sentence expresses this added idea?
items.instruction: 指出哪份摘要加了原文没有的观点，并抄出对应整句。
items.answer: Summary A；“Other software companies will probably soon develop products for African consumers.”
items.explanation: 原文只谈Microsoft与Google的行动，没有预测其他公司接下来会怎样。合理猜想也不能擅自写进摘要。另有频率误写：原文every two weeks，A写every day。

missions.instructions: 两段全部写Notes和单段Summary。原文、来源及段号全部给出；摘要可以不同，但不能改变原作者的时间、范围和语气。原页OCR将Schmid文章25段误识别为23段，已按图校正。
missions.answerNote: 提供两篇sample answers；不能只按范文措辞判分。

items.prompt: 原题 1：Original Passage 1
items.instruction: 写Notes关键词笔记，再用自己的词汇和句式写一个段落的摘要，只保留主旨和主要支撑，末尾加文内引用。
items.answer:
自编参考笔记：multilingual future; English important but not alone; non-English sites/resistance; English strong as second language; Mandarin possible demand in Asia
自编参考摘要：In the analysis reported by Schmid in 2004, English was expected to remain important without becoming the world’s only leading language. A more multilingual future, resistance to English dominance, and growth in non-English websites pointed toward a less exclusive role. English remained strong as a second language, while demand for Mandarin was expected to grow in parts of Asia (Schmid).
items.explanation: 原答案册提供可变样例，本参考进一步保留原文年代、可能性与范围：不把2004年的“未来十年”或2001年的“2050预测”当成今天事实，也不把亚洲部分雇主的需求夸大成全球必然趋势。

items.passage:
Source: Various paragraphs of a news article written by Randolph E. Schmid. It was published online by the Associated Press on February 26, 2004. The title of the article is “Share of people who are native English speakers declining.” The article is 25 paragraphs long. The Web site address is <http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/ap/571281251.html?did=571281251&FMT=ABS&FMTS=FT&date=Feb+26%2C+2004&author=RANDOLPH+E.+SCHMID&desc=Share+of+people+who+are+native+English+speakers+declining.

The world faces a future of people speaking more than one language, with English no longer seen as likely to become dominant, a British language expert says in a new analysis. “English is likely to remain one of the world’s most important languages for the foreseeable future, but its future is more problematic—and complex—than most people appreciate,” said language researcher David Graddol (Schmid, pars. 1-2). He sees English as likely to become the “first among equals” rather than having the global field to itself (par. 3). . . . The share of the world’s population that speaks English as a native language is falling, Graddol reports in a paper in Friday’s issue of the journal Science (par. 5). “There is a distinct consciousness in many countries, both developed and developing, about this dominance of English. There is some evidence of resistance to it, a desire to change it” said [Scott] Montgomery [the author of another article published in the same issue of Science]. For example, he said, in the early years of the Internet it was dominated by sites in English, but in recent years there has been a proliferation of non-English sites, especially Spanish, German, French, Japanese, and others (pars. 19-20). Nonetheless, English is strong as a second language, and teaching it has become a growth industry, said Montgomery, a Seattle-based geologist and energy consultant (par. 21). Graddol noted, though, that employers in parts of Asia are already looking beyond English. “In the next decade the new ‘must learn’ language is likely to be Mandarin” (par. 22).
rubric: 有关键词笔记和一段完整摘要。
保留两大主旨及必要限定，删去多数例证与重复。
用自己的语言，附(Schmid)或("World Empire")等能追溯的引用。

items.prompt: 原题 2：Original Passage 2
items.instruction: 写Notes关键词笔记，再用自己的词汇和句式写一个段落的摘要，只保留主旨和主要支撑，末尾加文内引用。
items.answer:
自编参考笔记：global spread; first/second/learning speakers; business/politics/Internet; predicted 2050 reach; difficult spelling/grammar/varieties/meaning
自编参考摘要：The 2001 article describes English as a global language used widely in business, politics, diplomacy, technology, and popular culture, with further growth predicted by 2050. Its international success does not make it easy to master: irregular forms, inconsistent spelling and pronunciation, regional varieties, and subtle changes in meaning can challenge even native speakers (“World Empire”).
items.explanation: 围绕“全球普及但不易精通”收束；不必把每个城市、每个set短语都列出。原文是2001年的文章，2050属于当时预测。无作者时引用简短题名，不能捏造作者。

items.passage:
Source: Paragraphs 1 and 2 from a December 20, 2001, online article entitled “A world empire by other means.” The author’s name is not given. It was published on Economist.com, the Web site of a British magazine. The Web site address is <http://www.economist.com/displaystory.cfm?story_id=S%26%2BXL%2FRA%5F%24%0A>

It [English] is everywhere. Some 380 million people speak it as their first language and perhaps two-thirds as many again as their second. A billion are learning it, about a third of the world’s population are in some sense exposed to it, and by 2050, it is predicted, half the world will be more or less proficient in it. It is the language of globalization—of international business, politics, and diplomacy. It is the language of computers and the Internet. You'll see it on posters in Côte d'Ivoire, you'll hear it in pop songs in Tokyo, you'll read it in official documents in Phnom Penh. Deutsche Welle broadcasts in it. Björk, an Icelander, sings in it. French business schools teach in it. It is the medium of expression in cabinet meetings in Bolivia. Truly, the tongue spoken back in the 1300s only by the “low people” of England, as Robert of Gloucester put it at the time, has come a long way. It is now the global language. How come? Not because English is easy. True, genders are simple, since English relies on “it” as the pronoun for all inanimate nouns, reserving masculine for bona fide males and feminine for females (and countries and ships). But the verbs tend to be irregular, the grammar bizarre, and the match between spelling and pronunciation a nightmare. English is now so widely spoken in so many places that umpteen versions have evolved, some so peculiar that even “native” speakers may have trouble understanding each other. But if only one version existed, that would present difficulties enough. Even everyday English is a language of subtlety, nuance, and complexity. John Simmons, a language consultant for Interbrand, likes to cite the word “set,” an apparently simple word that takes on different meanings in a sporting, cooking, social, or mathematical context—and that is before any little words are combined with it. Then, as a verb, it becomes “set aside,” “set up,” “set down,” “set in,” “set on,” “set about,” “set against,” and so on, terms that “leave even native speakers bewildered about [its] core meaning.”
rubric: 有关键词笔记和一段完整摘要。
保留两大主旨及必要限定，删去多数例证与重复。

items.prompt: 原题 Practice 6：Some people say that English is easy to learn, but difficult to master. Write a paragraph in which you agree with this statement.
items.instruction: 写一个赞同原题观点的完整段落，用Practice 5来源的摘要或部分摘要支撑；可加入自己的真实例子，并说明证据与主张的联系。
items.answer: 开放写作，无唯一答案。参考结构：清楚表达“英语可以较快入门，但精通需要持续练习”→选取来源关于不规则动词、拼写发音、多种英语或一词多义的摘要→用一个自身真实学习例子说明→归结为何基础交流与熟练掌握有差别。借用教材第二来源时引用(“World Empire”)，不要把作者预测冒充新调查。
items.explanation: 题目要写自己的论证段落，不是单独复述来源。比如“set在不同语境含义不同”可以支撑“难精通”，但必须解释这为什么超出基础交流。
